tickets.title: Service Status: Running / Status: Unknown
tickets.summary: You've installed the DHCP role on a new Domain Controller. The 'DHCP Server' service is started, but the management console shows a red down arrow on the IPv4 node. Clients are getting nothing.
artifact: Service Manager: DHCP Server Service is 'Running'
Console: IPv4 node shows a red down arrow icon.
tickets.debrief: Triage in Windows often requires looking past the 'Running' service status. Because DHCP is integrated with Active Directory, the service performs an 'environment check.' If it doesn't find itself in the Authorized Servers list, it will refuse to hand out IPs to prevent rogue server behavior. You successfully navigated from 'Service Status' to 'Security Authorization.'

triage.q: The service is 'Running' but the console is 'Red'. What is the most professional next step to identify the block?
options: Check the DHCP Audit Logs or the System Event Log for authorization errors
Restart the server to see if the icon turns green
Delete the scope and recreate it to reset the console status
Ping the gateway to check for network connectivity

diagnosis.q: You find Event ID 1046: 'The DHCP service is not authorized to start'. What is the root cause?
options: The DHCP service account has been locked out in AD
The server has not been granted permission to issue leases within the Active Directory forest
A rogue DHCP server has already claimed the subnet
The server's IP address is not static, which is required for authorization

fix.q: How do you resolve this 'Unauthorized' state?
options: Add the DHCP Server's computer account to the 'Domain Admins' group
Right-click 'DHCP' in the console and select 'Manage Authorized Servers' to add this node
Run 'netsh dhcp server initiate authorization'
Promote the server to a Global Catalog

tickets.title: The 'One-Way' Subnet
tickets.summary: A new satellite office (VLAN 20) was brought online. Users there can't get IPs. However, users in the HQ (VLAN 10), where the DHCP server sits, have no issues.
artifact: Router: Inter-VLAN routing is confirmed working for static IPs.
tickets.debrief: This illustrates the 'Broadcast Boundary' problem. DHCP 'Discovers' are broadcasts; routers kill broadcasts. By verifying that the server never saw the request, you correctly identified that the 'Request' never left the subnet. Configuring the IP Helper (Relay) on the router is the standard enterprise fix for this Layer 2 limitation.

triage.q: The DHCP server is healthy for HQ. What should you check to see if the Branch requests are even reaching the server?
options: Check the DHCP Server Statistics or a Packet Capture for 'DHCP Discovers' from the 10.10.20.x range
Check the Branch scope to see if it is 100% full
Check if the Branch users have the correct DNS settings
Check the DHCP 'Deny' filter list

diagnosis.q: The Packet Capture shows zero incoming traffic from the 10.10.20.0 subnet. What is the most likely architectural failure?
options: The DHCP server is too slow to respond to the remote subnet
The Branch Scope is deactivated
The Router/Switch is not configured to relay DHCP broadcasts across VLAN boundaries
The DHCP server doesn't have a NIC physically plugged into the Branch VLAN

fix.q: What is the industry-standard remediation for this?
options: Install a local DHCP server at the Branch office
Configure an 'IP Helper-Address' (DHCP Relay) on the Branch VLAN's gateway interface
Create a Superscope that combines VLAN 10 and VLAN 20
Change the subnet mask of the HQ scope to include the Branch range
